description: Mapping dictionary for localizing global Yelp review keywords and sentiments into Nigerian cultural touchpoints and Pidgin expressions.

mappings.description: A casual local spot where people gather after work to drink lager beer, talk politics, and eat side dishes like pepper soup or point-and-kill fish.
mappings.example_global: We met up at the local pub after work for a few pints.
mappings.example_nigerian_pidgin: We hook up for one beer parlour after work to chill.

mappings.description: A small, informal dining spot serving local staple dishes (e.g., amala, pounded yam, jollof rice) quickly and affordably, often managed by a head cook referred to as 'Mama'.
mappings.example_global: We stopped by a small corner bistro for a quick lunch.
mappings.example_nigerian_pidgin: We branch one nice Buka for road side eat beta amala.

mappings.pidgin_equivalent: Get pepper / Pepper go kill person
mappings.description: Refers to high heat levels from hot peppers (like habanero/atarodo). In Nigerian cuisine, spice is a baseline expectation, and 'spicy' foods are appreciated for their throat-clearing heat.
mappings.example_global: The sauce was delicious but a bit too spicy for my taste.
mappings.example_nigerian_pidgin: The soup sweet well-well but the pepper dey active.

mappings.description: Chapman is Nigeria's signature non-alcoholic/alcoholic cocktail, made with Fanta, Sprite, Angostura bitters, blackcurrant cordial, and cucumber garnish. Essential at any event.
mappings.example_global: I ordered a fruity summer cocktail at the bar.
mappings.example_nigerian_pidgin: I tell the steward make he bring cold Chapman for me.

mappings.description: Usually addressed formally as 'Steward' or 'Server'. In highly informal settings, users might refer to them as 'attendant'. Address style is crucial for showing respect.
mappings.example_global: Our waiter was very attentive and prompt.
mappings.example_nigerian_pidgin: The steward dey try, he dey quick response to our call.

mappings.nigerian_cultural_touchpoint: Oga / Manager / Oga at the top
mappings.pidgin_equivalent: Oga / Oga at the top / Madam
mappings.description: The boss or supervisor. Escalating an issue to the 'Oga' is a standard move when service fails.
mappings.example_global: We asked to speak to the manager about the bill.
mappings.example_nigerian_pidgin: We ask to see the Oga because of the money response.

mappings.description: Expression of extreme food satisfaction. 'Sweet' is the universal pidgin translation for tasty/delicious.
mappings.example_global: The steak was absolutely delicious and cooked perfectly.
mappings.example_nigerian_pidgin: The food sweet die, everything correct.

mappings.pidgin_equivalent: My eye clear / I vex / Money waste
mappings.description: Expressing deep regret or anger at poor service or food quality, usually leading to a vow never to return.
mappings.example_global: I was highly disappointed by the cold food and bad service.
mappings.example_nigerian_pidgin: I vex well-well as they bring cold food, my money waste.

mappings.description: High pricing that feels unjustified, often described as 'over-billing' or 'tearing pocket'.
mappings.example_global: The entrees were overpriced and not worth the cost.
mappings.example_nigerian_pidgin: The price of food for there dey tear pocket, e no worth am.

mappings.description: Frustration with slow service. Nigerians despise waiting long for food unless they are hanging out at a joint.
mappings.example_global: We had to wait for 45 minutes for our table.
mappings.example_nigerian_pidgin: We stand for line like 45 minutes, na long thing o.

mappings.description: Concept of eating a heavy meal in the late morning (e.g. Yam and Egg, Akara and Pap, or Noodles) that serves as both breakfast and lunch.
mappings.example_global: We went out for a nice Sunday brunch.
mappings.example_nigerian_pidgin: We branch out for late heavy breakfast of yam and egg.

mappings.description: Sweet items eaten after a meal, often equated conceptually to 'sweet mouth' (craving something sweet) or associated with puff-puff and small chops at gatherings.
mappings.example_global: We finished our dinner with a chocolate dessert.
mappings.example_nigerian_pidgin: After we chop, we use puff-puff take sweet mouth.
